newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB's Meyer says Swiss need cautious growth.
newsitem.headline: SNB's Meyer says Swiss need cautious growth.

text.p: Swiss National Bank (SNB) president Hans Meyer said the country's sluggish economy needs a cautious return to growth, the Swiss news agency SDA reported.
Meyer told members of the Swiss parlaiment that the country should continue raising productivity and value-added production but that structural reforms should be socially acceptable.
"Switzerland must find a way back to economic growth. But it must be a cautious growth," SDA quoted Meyer as saying in a briefing on economic isues for Radical Democratic (FDP) members of parliament.
Meyer was speaking after gross domestic product (GDP) data that showed Swiss GDP fell 0.9 percent in the second quarter of 1996 from the first quarter of 1996, the sixth quarterly decline in a row.

Meyer repeated that the Swiss National Bank had done all it could to help boost growth by lowering the discount rate. The SNB made four cuts from late 1994 through last December, when the discount rate was lowered to the current 1.5 percent.
"More than a year ago, we started a loosening of monetary policy. We have done what had to be done and what could be done," Meyer said. -- Zurich Newsroom, +41-1-631 7340
